'''Ami Elizabeth Radunskaya''' is an American mathematician and musician. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Pomona College]], where she specializes in [[dynamical system]]s and the applications of [[mathematics]] to medicine,<ref name="pres"/> such as the use of [[cellular automaton|cellular automata]] to model [[drug delivery]].<ref>{{citation|title=Math Modeling a Better World|publisher=Claremont Graduate University|url=http://www.cgu.edu/pages/9899.asp|magazine=The Flame|accessdate=December 15, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220143213/http://www.cgu.edu/pages/9899.asp|archive-date=December 20, 2016|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}.</ref>  In 2016 she was elected as the president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM).<ref name="pres">{{citation|url=https://www.pomona.edu/news/2016/03/09-pomona-math-prof-ami-radunskaya-elected-president-association-women-mathematics|title=Pomona Math Prof. Ami Radunskaya Elected President of the Association for Women in Mathematics|publisher=Pomona College|date=March 9, 2016|first=April Xiaoyi|last=Xu|access-date=December 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820171832/https://www.pomona.edu/news/2016/03/09-pomona-math-prof-ami-radunskaya-elected-president-association-women-mathematics|archive-date=August 20, 2019|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Early life and music==
Radunskaya, the daughter of a [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]] economist, began playing the [[cello]] as a 9-year-old. After graduating from high school at the age of 16,<ref name="role">{{citation|title=How to Become a Role Model for Women in Math: The inspiring stubbornness of Pomona College Professor of Math Ami Radunskaya|magazine=Pomona College Magazine|date=February 23, 2015|url=http://magazine.pomona.edu/2015/spring/how-to-become-a-role-model-for-women-in-math/}}.</ref> she took ten years off from her education to work as cellist and [[composer|music composer]],<ref name="pres"/> including seven years as a member of the [[Oakland Symphony]].<ref name="role"/> As "a well known Bay Area cellist specializing in new music", she "performed throughout the U.S. and Europe with [[Don Buchla]]."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/5100254/|newspaper=Ukiah Daily Journal|date=November 26, 1980|title=Arch Ensemble in coast concert|department=That's entertainment|quote=The program at the Mendocino Arts Center will include the world premiere of San Francisco Bay Area artist Ami Radunskaya's "Tête-à-tête." ... Ms. Radunskaya, a well known Bay Area cellist specializing in new music, has performed throughout the U.S. and Europe with Don Buchla. Ms. Radunskaya is a member of the Arch Ensemble.}}</ref> In the late 1970s, [[Buchla Electronic Musical Instruments]] made a custom [[synthesizer]] for her, the "Sili-Con Cello",<ref>[http://www.vintagesynth.com/misc/buchla200.php Buchla 200 Series], Vintage Synth Explorer, retrieved December 13, 2016.</ref><ref>{{citation|contribution=A history of Buchla's musical instruments|last=Buchla|first=Don|authorlink=Don Buchla|title=Proceedings of the 2005 International Conference on New Interfaces for Musical Expression (NIME05)|url=http://www.nime.org/proceedings/2005/nime2005_001.pdf}}.</ref> and several of her works use the [[Radiodrum|radio baton]], a controller for electronic music devices in the form of a conductor's baton.<ref>{{citation|title=The infinite crescendo|first=Chantelle|last=Oligschlaeger|magazine=[[Compute!]]|date=December 1991|url=http://www.atarimagazines.com/compute/issue136/114_The_infinite_crescen.php|issue=136}}.</ref> One of her cello and radio baton compositions, "A Wild and Reckless Place" (1990), is known for its use of the [[Bohlen–Pierce scale]].<ref>{{citation|title=Discography of Microtonal CDs|publisher=Huygens-Fokker Foundation|accessdate=December 13, 2016|url=http://www.huygens-fokker.org/music/discography.html}}.</ref><ref>{{citation | last = Hooker | first = J. N. | contribution = Finding Alternative Musical Scales | doi = 10.1007/978-3-319-44953-1_47 | pages = 753–768 | publisher = [[Springer Publishing|Springer]] | series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science | title = International Conference on Principles and Practice of Constraint Programming (CP 2016) | volume = 9892 | year = 2016 | contribution-url = http://web.tepper.cmu.edu/jnh/scales2.pdf | isbn = 978-3-319-44952-4 | access-date = December 14, 2016 | archive-date = December 20, 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161220123659/http://web.tepper.cmu.edu/jnh/scales2.pdf | url-status = dead }}.</ref>

==Education==
Radunskaya did her undergraduate studies at the [[University of California, Berkeley]],<ref name="pres"/> as a single mother. There, she studied [[computer science]] and [[chemistry]] before eventually majoring in [[mathematics]].<ref name="role"/> She completed her doctorate in mathematics at [[Stanford University]] in 1992, under the supervision of [[Donald Samuel Ornstein]]; her dissertation was titled ''Statistical Properties of Deterministic Bernoulli Flows''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=39238}}</ref>

== Mathematics career ==
After postdoctoral studies at [[Rice University]], she joined the [[Pomona College]] faculty in 1994.<ref name="role" /> In June 2022, the college announced her appointment as the Lingurn H. Burkhead Professor of Mathematics, an [[endowed chair]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harry |first=Lorraine Wu |date=2022-06-13 |title=Nine Faculty Members Appointed to Endowed Professorships |url=https://www.pomona.edu/news/2022/06/14-nine-faculty-members-appointed-endowed-professorships |access-date=2022-06-25 |website= |publisher=Pomona College |language=en}}</ref>
==Awards and honors==
Radunskaya was the [[AWM/MAA Falconer Lecturer]] for 2010, speaking on "Mathematical Challenges in the Treatment of Cancer".<ref name="aaas"/><ref>Mathematical Challenges in the Treatment of Cancer, Past Falconer Lectures, AWM, retrieved December 13, 2016.</ref> In 2016 she was named as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to mathematical oncology, immuno-dynamics, and applications of dynamical systems to medicine, and for service to the mathematical community."<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2017 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], accessed December 12, 2016.</ref> She also won the Mentor Award of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] for her work as a founder and director of the [[EDGE Foundation]], a national program that encourages women to study mathematics at the graduate level.<ref name="aaas">{{citation|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/mathematician-ami-radunskaya-wins-2016-aaas-mentor-award|title=Mathematician Ami Radunskaya Wins 2016 AAAS Mentor Award|publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|date=November 29, 2016|first=Ginger|last=Pinholster}}.</ref> Radunskaya was president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM) from February 2017 to January 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=AWM History|url=https://awm-math.org/about/history/|last=|first=|date=May 16, 2020|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191101004308/https://awm-math.org/about/history/ |archive-date=November 1, 2019 |access-date=}}</ref> She was selected as a Fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the Class of 2021 "''for her career-long efforts to invite women into our profession by learning about people’s individual journeys and driving the community to be more welcoming of diverse pathways into mathematics via her work during her AWM presidency and as co-director of the Enhancing Diversity in Graduate Education summer program''."<ref name=awmfellow>{{cite web |title=The AWM Fellows Program: 2021 Class of AWM Fellows |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2021-awm-fellows/ |publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics |accessdate=7 November 2020}}</ref> Radunskaya gave the opening plenary lecture at the 2022 AWM Research Symposium.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 AWM Research Symposium Schedule of Events |url=https://awm-math.org/meetings/awm-research-symposium/awm-research-symposium-2022-schedule/ |access-date=June 19, 2022}}</ref> She also received the Alfred Gores Award for Excellence in Teaching in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-06-01 |title=Ami E. Radunskaya {{!}} Pomona College in Claremont, California - Pomona College |url=https://www.pomona.edu/directory/people/ami-e-radunskaya |access-date=2025-09-23 |website=www.pomona.edu |language=en}}</ref> She won the Wig Distinguished Professor Award In May 2024, at Pomona College.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-10 |title=Pomona College Faculty Recognized for Excellence in Teaching, Service {{!}} Pomona College in Claremont, California - Pomona College |url=https://www.pomona.edu/news/2024/05/13-pomona-college-faculty-recognized-excellence-teaching-service |access-date=2025-10-08 |website=www.pomona.edu |language=en}}</ref>
